sentences.en: So the Powell Doctrine essentially held that first one had to exhaust all diplomatic options, then to determine just what a path to victory would be,

sentences.en: And after having achieved all of those things, then to go in with, to use his phrase, overwhelming force,

sentences.zh: 在9·11事件发生的紧要关头，首先要确定是谁袭击了我们。

sentences.en: So, Robert, help us understand the role that Powell ends up playing in the military campaign that came to define his tenure as Secretary of State, the invasion of Iraq after 9-11.
sentences.zh: 那是基地组织。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 这导致向阿富汗部署军队以清剿塔利班。

sentences.en: In the immediate wake of September 11th, there was first a determination of who it was that attacked us.
sentences.zh: 随后布什将注意力转向了他所描述的反恐战争的下一个战区。

sentences.en: That was al-Qaeda.
sentences.zh: 这并不是鲍威尔国务卿脑子里想的事情。

sentences.en: And this led to the deployment of troops to Afghanistan to rout the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 他认为在9·11事件之后，我们只有一个明确的目标，

sentences.en: Then Bush turned his attention to what he described as the next theater in the war on terror.
sentences.zh: 那就是追剿像袭击世贸中心和五角大楼那样的恐怖组织。

sentences.en: Now, this was not something that Secretary Powell had in mind.
sentences.zh: 但布什心里想的却是萨达姆·侯赛因。

sentences.en: He assumed that in the wake of September 11th, we had one clear objective,
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: and that was to go after terrorist organizations like the ones that had attacked the World Trade Center and the Pentagon.
sentences.zh: 嗯，布什开始谈论入侵伊拉克的可能性，首先是因为他认为萨达姆·侯赛因是个坏演员，我想有几个原因。

sentences.en: But Bush had Saddam Hussein in mind instead.
sentences.zh: 他记得萨达姆·侯赛因就是那个情报机构在1993年曾试图暗杀他父亲乔治·赫伯特·沃克·布什的人。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 其次，他也指出，在9·11事件发生的直接后果中，

sentences.en: Well, Bush started talking about the possibility of invading Iraq because, first of all, he viewed Saddam Hussein as a bad actor, I think for a couple of reasons.
sentences.zh: 当世界上几乎所有国家（包括伊朗）都表示声援美国时，

sentences.en: He remembered Saddam Hussein as the person whose intelligence service had apparently attempted to assassinate his father,
sentences.zh: 只有伊拉克在一旁冷嘲热讽美国，基本上是在说“这是你们咎由自取”。

sentences.en: George Herbert Walker Bush, in 1993.
sentences.zh: 事实上，萨达姆在9月12日发表了一场演讲，其中他表示美国自食了其自身外交政策的苦果。

sentences.en: And secondly, he also noted that in the immediate aftermath of September 11th,
sentences.zh: 因此，布什在国情咨文中发表了一场演讲，即著名的“邪恶轴心”演讲，

sentences.en: when pretty much every country in the world, including Iran, indicated solidarity towards the United States,
sentences.zh: 他在演讲中点名了萨达姆和伊拉克，并暗示他们是恐怖主义支持国。

sentences.en: Iraq stood alone in kind of jeering the U.S., essentially saying, you had it coming to you.
sentences.zh: 因此，他不仅向萨达姆，而且向美国和全世界发出警告，表明萨达姆已经在他的雷达上了。

sentences.en: Saddam, in fact, did give a speech on September the 12th in which he said that America has reaped the thorns of its own foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 事实上，萨达姆在9月12日确实发表过一次演讲，他在其中表示美国自食了其外交政策的恶果。

sentences.en: So Bush gave a speech at the State of the Union Address, the famous Axis of Evil speech,
sentences.zh: 因此布什在国情咨文中发表了一场演讲，也就是著名的“邪恶轴心”演讲，

sentences.en: in which he called out Saddam and Iraq and indicated that they were state sponsors of terror.
sentences.zh: 他在演讲中点名了萨达姆和伊拉克，并暗示他们是恐怖主义的国家资助者。

sentences.en: So he was not only putting Saddam but really the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，他不仅是在向萨达姆，也是在向美国

sentences.en: and the world on notice that Saddam was on his radar.
sentences.zh: 乃至全世界发出警告，表明萨达姆已经进入了他的视线。

sentences.en: Now, Powell kind of figured, like a lot of people in the foreign policy establishment, that Saddam did have some weapons capacity.
sentences.zh: 当时，鲍威尔和许多外交政策建制派人士一样，认为萨达姆确实具备一定的武器生产能力。

sentences.en: But he also believed that Saddam didn't pose a threat to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但他同时也认为萨达姆对美国并不构成威胁。

sentences.en: This put him in direct opposition with Dick Cheney, the vice president, the secretary of defense, Donald Rumsfeld, and Bush himself.
sentences.zh: 这使他与副总统迪克·切尼、国防部长唐纳德·拉姆斯费尔德以及小布什本人产生了直接分歧。

sentences.en: Powell began to realize that he was really an outside man looking in,
sentences.zh: 鲍威尔开始意识到，自己实际上成了一个被边缘化的局外人，

sentences.en: that the guy who had been brought in to be this credible force in foreign policy for this fledgling administration was now a guy who was not influencing foreign policy at all.
sentences.zh: 当初被请进这个崭新的政府、作为外交政策中坚力量的那个人，如今却根本无法对外交政策产生任何影响。

sentences.en: So once this realization dawns on Powell that Bush wants to go to war and that he thinks that's a terrible idea, what does he do?
sentences.zh: 因此，一旦鲍威尔意识到布什执意要发动战争，并且他认为这是一个极其糟糕的想法时，他会怎么做呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I spent a lot of time as someone who wrote a book on this subject looking at this window of the summer and fall of 2002
sentences.zh: 是的，作为一名曾就此主题写过书的学者，我花了很多时间研究2002年夏秋之际的那段时期，

sentences.en: when Powell begins to realize that he's kind of the outside man looking in and needs to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 当时鲍威尔开始意识到自己有点像个局外人，并觉得必须为此做点什么。

sentences.en: And so what he does is he reaches out to Bush's friend and national security advisor Condoleezza Rice and says, I want a meeting with the president.
sentences.zh: 于是他联系了布什的朋友兼国家安全顾问康多莉扎·赖斯，表示想和总统见个面。

sentences.en: So it was Powell who, on August 5, 2002, had this dinner in the White House residence with the president.
sentences.zh: 所以在2002年8月5日，正是鲍威尔在白宫官邸与总统共进晚餐。

sentences.en: And it was an interesting conversation, interesting for one thing in its singularity,
sentences.zh: 那是一次很有意思的对话，其独特性尤其引人注目，

sentences.en: because there was no one else up to this point, and for that matter, no one else after this point who Bush would hear from in his administration who would say,
sentences.zh: 因为在此之前没有其他人，而且在此之后在布什政府里也没有任何人曾对布什直言：

sentences.en: you know, there's a lot of bad things that could happen if you invade Iraq.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果入侵伊拉克，可能会发生很多糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: And so it was Powell who basically said, if you do this, Mr. President, you will become the proud owner of a country and its 20 or so fractious provinces.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上是鲍威尔说：如果你这么做，总统先生，你将成为一个国家及其大约二十个分裂省份的骄傲主人。

sentences.en: Essentially, you know, if you break it, you will own it.
sentences.zh: 本质上讲，你知道的，你把它弄坏了，你就得买单。

sentences.en: It seems like what he's saying is this will not at all be a Powell doctrine-like war.
sentences.zh: 听起来他的意思是，这绝对不会是一场符合“鲍威尔主义”的战争。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, he was saying that it instead could be a mess.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是说这反而会是一场烂摊子。

sentences.en: And Bush then said to Powell, well, what should I do?
sentences.zh: 布什随后对鲍威尔说，那我该怎么做？

sentences.en: And he said, go to the United Nations.
sentences.zh: 他说，去联合国吧。

sentences.en: Build a coalition through the UN.
sentences.zh: 通过联合国建立一个联盟。

sentences.en: Have them pass a resolution that will have weapon inspectors go in.
sentences.zh: 让他们通过一项决议，允许武器核查人员进入。

sentences.en: And ultimately, he heeded what Powell's advice was.
sentences.zh: 最终，他听取了鲍威尔的建议。

sentences.en: And Powell believed coming out of that meeting and in the weeks and months to follow that he had succeeded.
sentences.zh: 鲍威尔在走出那次会面后，以及在随后的几周和几个月里，都相信自己成功了。

sentences.en: But Bush got very impatient during that whole process.
sentences.zh: 但布什在整个过程中变得非常不耐烦。

sentences.en: So in January 2003, Bush comes to Colin Powell and he said, you know what?
sentences.zh: 因此在2003年1月，布什找到科林·鲍威尔说，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I think I have to do this.
sentences.zh: 我想我不得不这么做了。

sentences.en: I think I have to invade Iraq.
sentences.zh: 我想我必须入侵伊拉克。

sentences.en: Are you with me?
sentences.zh: 你支持我吗？

sentences.en: And what do you think Bush meant by that?
sentences.zh: 你觉得布什这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, it's important to note first, Michael, that Bush had already at that point stated his intentions to invade Iraq with his national security advisor, Condoleezza Rice,
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，首先需要指出的是，当时布什已经向国家安全顾问康多莉扎·赖斯、

sentences.en: with Vice President Dick Cheney, and with Secretary of Defense Donald Rumsfeld.
sentences.zh: 副总统迪克·切尼以及国防部长唐纳德·拉姆斯费尔德表明了自己入侵伊拉克的意图。

sentences.en: So in essence, what Bush was saying was, look, I need to do this and I need to know that I have your support.
sentences.zh: 所以从本质上讲，布什的意思是：听着，我必须这么做，我需要知道我有你的支持。

sentences.en: I need you essentially to drop your concerns and be with me on this.
sentences.zh: 我需要你基本上放下顾虑，在这件事上与我站在一起。

sentences.en: Now, when Powell heard this, he said, yes, sir, I'm with you, very much in the manner of the four-star general that he was.
sentences.zh: 当鲍威尔听到这话时，他回答说：遵命，长官，我支持你，完全表现出他作为一名四星上将的作风。

sentences.en: And indeed, when I discussed this matter with Powell, he said to me, what was I going to do?
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我与鲍威尔讨论这件事时，他对我说：我当时能怎么办？

sentences.en: He was the commander-in-chief after all.
sentences.zh: 他毕竟是三军统帅。

sentences.en: But then Powell went on to add, but you know, people call me the reluctant warrior, but in fact, in the end, I'm a warrior.
sentences.zh: 但鲍威尔接着补充道，不过你知道，人们叫我勉强参战的战士，但事实上，到头来我就是个战士。

sentences.en: And so if you're going to go to war, I'm a guy to have with you.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你要打仗，我就是那个适合陪你上战场的人。

sentences.en: Powell was essentially saying that at the time he was thinking, if Bush is going to go to war, he's going to need me to supervise this war for him.
sentences.zh: 鲍威尔当时的本意是想，如果布什执意要开战，他会需要我来替他监督这场战争。

sentences.en: Even if it's a war he did not at all support.
sentences.zh: 即便这是一场他根本不支持的战争。

sentences.en: He wanted to be the one to oversee it.
sentences.zh: 他希望成为那个监督战争的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, he wanted to make sure that if Bush was going to go to war, that it would be a war done in the most efficacious manner possible by the author of the Powell Doctrine.
sentences.zh: 是的，他希望确保如果布什要开战，那也将是一场由“鲍威尔主义”的鼻祖以最高效的方式进行的战争。

sentences.en: And so once he makes this decision to be the reluctant warrior, to sign on to a war he does not think will work out well for the U.S.,
sentences.zh: 因此，一旦他做出决定成为那个勉强参战的战士、去支持一场他认为对美国不会有好结果的战争时，

sentences.en: what does it start to look like and what role does he play in it?
sentences.zh: 事情会变成什么样子？他在其中扮演了什么角色？

sentences.en: Well, something that I think that Powell hadn't anticipated, which was that as it turned out, he was not asked to supervise the war, to conduct the war.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为有一点是鲍威尔没有预料到的，那就是事实证明，他没有被要求去监督战争、指挥战争。

sentences.en: He was asked to sell the war.
sentences.zh: 他被要求去兜售这场战争。

sentences.en: And this became clear in the latter part of January of that same month in 2003,
sentences.zh: 这一点在2003年1月下旬变得明朗起来，

sentences.en: when Powell was asked by Condoleezza Rice on behalf of President Bush if Powell would give a major speech to the United Nations and make the case for war based on the intelligence findings that the American intelligence community had.
sentences.zh: 当时康多莉扎·赖斯代表布什总统询问鲍威尔，是否愿意在联合国发表一次重要演讲，并根据美国情报界的情报调查结果为战争寻找理由。

sentences.en: Vice President Cheney, in fact, reinforced this to Powell, saying to him, in essence, look, Colin, you've got more popularity than the rest of us put together.
sentences.zh: 事实上，副总统切尼也向鲍威尔强调了这一点，他的意思Basically是：听着，科林，你的声望比我们所有人的总和还要高。

sentences.en: Why don't you spend some political capital?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不消耗一些政治资本呢？

sentences.en: And once again, Powell, I think being an enormously self-confident man, also believed that he was the right guy for that.
sentences.zh: 再次我认为，鲍威尔作为一个极度自信的人，也相信自己是不二人选。

sentences.en: He was, after all, the chief diplomat of the United States.
sentences.zh: 他毕竟是美国的首席外交官。

sentences.en: He also believed that he could issue more restraint in his speech and make a fact-based presentation in a way that others in the administration could not.
sentences.zh: 他还相信，自己可以在演讲中表现得更加克制，并以政府中其他人无法做到的方式进行基于事实的陈述。

sentences.en: So how does he approach this speech?
sentences.zh: 那么他是如何看待这场演讲的？

sentences.en: What is Powell's thinking?
sentences.zh: 鲍威尔是怎么想的？

sentences.en: So what Powell did was he was handed a kind of a working draft of the speech that had been compiled by the vice president's office.
sentences.zh: 因此，鲍威尔拿到了一份由副总统办公室汇编的演讲初稿，

sentences.en: He basically thumbed through it, had some of his own intelligence experts take a look at it, and ultimately tossed it in the garbage can and said, nope,
sentences.zh: 他基本上翻阅了一下，让自己的情报专家过目，最后直接把它扔进了垃圾桶并说：不行，

sentences.en: we're starting from scratch.
sentences.zh: 我们要从头开始。

sentences.en: This has got too many outlandish claims to it.
sentences.zh: 这里面有太多荒谬的说法了。

sentences.en: He then spent a long weekend at CIA headquarters in a conference room.
sentences.zh: 随后他在中央情报局总部的一个会议室里度过了一个漫长的周末。

sentences.en: He and a speech writer surrounded by intelligence analysts and just went through the intelligence piece by piece, basically deciding, okay, what can we credibly say?
sentences.zh: 他和一位演讲稿撰写人被情报分析师们包围着，逐条审阅情报，基本上在决定：好吧，我们能可信地说些什么？

sentences.en: What do we really know about Saddam's weapons program?
sentences.zh: 我们对萨达姆的武器计划到底了解多少？

sentences.en: And through this process, he kept a lot of really dubious intel out of the speech.
sentences.zh: 通过这个过程，他将许多非常可疑的情报剔除出了演讲。

sentences.en: And by the end of it all, believed that through this process, had a speech now with rock-solid intelligence that attested to not just Saddam's weapons capability,
sentences.zh: 到最后，他相信通过这个过程，演讲中已经有了坚如磐石的情报，不仅能证明萨达姆的武器能力，

sentences.en: but to the weapons he actually had at his disposal at that point.
sentences.zh: 还能证明他当时实际拥有的武器。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's where things stand as Colin Powell heads over to the UN to deliver a speech I know I watched and that everybody else I know in the media was watching that day.
sentences.zh: 好了，这就是科林·鲍威尔前往联合国发表那次演讲时的情景，我知道我看了，而且那天我认识的所有媒体同行也都在看。

sentences.en: I call now on the distinguished Secretary of State, Mr. Colin Powell.
sentences.zh: 我现在请尊敬的国务卿科林·鲍威尔先生发言。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's where things stood when on February the 5th, 2003...
sentences.zh: 是的，在2003年2月5日事情就是这样的……

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，总统先生。

sentences.en: Mr. President, Mr. Secretary General...
sentences.zh: 总统先生，秘书长先生……

sentences.en: The Secretary of State made it to the United Nations...
sentences.zh: 国务卿来到了联合国……

sentences.en: The gravity of this moment is matched by the gravity of the threat that Iraq's weapons of mass destruction pose to the world.
sentences.zh: 这一时刻的严重性与伊拉克大规模杀伤性武器对世界构成的威胁的严重性相当。

sentences.en: And gave a lengthy, seemingly evidentiary-based recitation of Saddam's weapons program.
sentences.zh: 他发表了一场冗长的、看似基于证据的对萨达姆武器计划的陈述。

sentences.en: Let me now turn to those deadly weapons programs and describe why they are real and present dangers to the region and to the world.
sentences.zh: 现在让我转向那些致命的武器计划，并阐述为什么它们对该地区和世界构成了现实且紧迫的威胁。

sentences.en: First, biological weapons.
sentences.zh: 首先，是生化武器。

sentences.en: Among the things that Powell said was that Saddam had an active biological weapons program.
sentences.zh: 鲍威尔所说的话之一是萨达姆拥有一个活跃的生物武器计划。

sentences.en: One of the most worrisome things that emerges from the thick intelligence file we have on Iraq's biological weapons is the existence of mobile production facilities used to make biological agents.
sentences.zh: 在我们关于伊拉克生物武器的大量情报档案中，最令人担忧的事情之一就是存在用于制造生物剂的移动生产设施。

sentences.en: Consisting of mobile biological laboratories that had been undetectable by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 包括美国一直无法检测到的移动生物实验室。

sentences.en: If biological weapons seem too terrible to contemplate, chemical weapons are equally chilling.
sentences.zh: 如果说生物武器看起来已经让人难以想象的恐怖，那么化学武器同样令人不寒而栗。

sentences.en: Saddam Hussein has never accounted for vast amounts of chemical weaponry.
sentences.zh: 萨达姆·侯赛因从未对大量的化学武器做出过交代。

sentences.en: And that Saddam was pumping out an alarming amount of chemical weapons, also in contravention of the United Nations.
sentences.zh: 萨达姆还在源源不断地生产令人惊慌数量的化学武器，这也是对联合国的公然违反。

sentences.en: Our conservative estimate is that Iraq today has a stockpile of between 100 and 500 tons of chemical weapons agents.
sentences.zh: 我们保守估计，伊拉克目前拥有100至500吨化学武器剂的库存。

sentences.en: That is enough agent to cause mass casualties across more than 100 square miles of territory, an area nearly five times the size of Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 这些武器足以在超过100平方英里的领土上造成大规模伤亡，这一面积几乎是曼哈顿的五倍。

sentences.en: And that Saddam possessed the capacity to develop a nuclear program owing to some aluminum tubes that had been seized that could be used for nuclear centrifuges.
sentences.zh: 由于缴获了一些可用于核离心机的铝管，萨达姆拥有了开发核计划的能力。

sentences.en: We have no indication that Saddam Hussein has ever abandoned his nuclear weapons program.
sentences.zh: 我们没有任何迹象表明萨达姆·侯赛因曾放弃过他的核武器计划。

sentences.en: On the contrary, we have more than a decade of proof that he remains determined to acquire nuclear weapons.
sentences.zh: 恰恰相反，我们有十多年的证据表明他依然决意获得核武器。

sentences.en: In essence, what Powell was saying was a kind of nightmare scenario, that Saddam already had weapons of mass destruction and, worst of all,
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，鲍威尔所说的是一种噩梦般的场景，即萨达姆已经拥有了大规模杀伤性武器，最糟糕的是，

sentences.en: was intent on developing an active nuclear program as well.
sentences.zh: 他还执意要开发一个活跃的核计划。

sentences.en: We must not shrink from whatever is ahead of us.
sentences.zh: 无论前方有什么，我们都绝不能退缩。

sentences.en: We must not fail on our duty and our responsibility to the citizens of the countries that are represented by this body.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不能辜负我们对本机构所代表国家公民的义务和责任。

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，总统先生。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The message was Saddam Hussein is a threat, an urgent threat to the United States, and there is justification for war.
sentences.zh: 传递的信息是，萨达姆·侯赛因是一个威胁，是对美国的紧迫威胁，开战是有正当理由的。

sentences.en: And I think, Michael, that anyone who wasn't a real student of the intelligence tended to come to the conclusion you just described.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我认为任何不是情报真正研究者的人，往往都会得出你刚刚描述的结论。

sentences.en: Certainly that was the case on Capitol Hill, where, for example, the Democratic leader Tom Daschle said to his Senate caucus,
sentences.zh: 国会山的情况当然也是如此，例如民主党领袖汤姆·达施勒对他的参议院党团成员说：

sentences.en: look, I know you guys don't believe Vice President Cheney, but surely you believe Colin Powell.
sentences.zh: 听着，我知道你们不相信副总统切尼，但你们总该相信科林·鲍威尔吧。

sentences.en: The sheer, dry elaboration of this weapons program, delivered by someone who seemed once again to be in his element,
sentences.zh: 这种纯粹的、干巴巴的对武器计划的详细阐述，由一个似乎再次游刃有余的人讲出来，

sentences.en: giving basically the most important speech of his career and seeming at the time to be thoroughly up to the task, was itself as persuasive as the evidence that he was presenting.
sentences.zh: 他发表了其职业生涯中最重要的一次演讲，并且当时看起来完全能够胜任这一任务，这本身就和他在展示的证据一样具有说服力。

sentences.en: So Bush was right to understand that Powell's stature and popularity, and Powell's stature and popularity alone,
sentences.zh: 因此，布什的理解是正确的：鲍威尔的声望和人气，仅仅依靠鲍威尔的声望和人气，

sentences.en: could overcome the skepticism of even congressional Democrats about this war.
sentences.zh: 就能克服国会民主党人对这场战争的怀疑。

sentences.en: Absolutely, yeah.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: For the Secretary of State, who had been urging a diplomatic path, who had been talking about going to the United Nations,
sentences.zh: 对于这位一直主张走外交道路、一直谈论去联合国的国务卿来说，

sentences.en: to make the presentation that he did was itself an indicator to some people who'd been on the fence that, okay, it now makes sense to go to war.
sentences.zh: 能够做出那样的陈述，本身就向那些原本态度摇摆的人释放了一个信号：好吧，现在开战是合情合理的了。

sentences.en: And then, of course, the United States invades Iraq, and we eventually learned that all of that intel, all of that evidence that Powell has used in this speech was totally false,
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，美国入侵了伊拉克，我们最终得知，所有的情报，鲍威尔在演讲中使用的所有证据全都是假的，

sentences.en: and that U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国的

sentences.en: intelligence agencies had gotten it wrong.
sentences.zh: 情报机构搞错了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What Powell came to realize woefully after the fact was that that weekend when he was putting the speech together,
sentences.zh: 事后鲍威尔痛苦地意识到，那个周末当他被情报分析师们包围着整理演讲稿时，

sentences.en: surrounded by intelligence analysts, that what the analysts were basically spouting to him
sentences.zh: 分析师们向他滔滔不绝灌输的那些结论，

sentences.en: were conclusions that were the result of years and years of groupthink that had not been challenged, that there had been a leaning into worst-case scenarios about what Saddam had,
sentences.zh: 其实是多年来未经质疑的群体思维的结果，他们倾向于对萨达姆拥有的东西做出最坏的设想，

sentences.en: when in fact there was no evidence, literally none, of what Saddam did have.
sentences.zh: 而事实上根本没有证据，可以说是毫无证据来证明萨达姆到底拥有什么。

sentences.en: It was all based on suppositions.
sentences.zh: 这一切都建立在猜测的基础之上。

sentences.en: And that somehow all of the nuance, all the caveats had been loSt.
sentences.zh: 不知何故，所有的细微差别和警告都被淹没了。

sentences.en: And what ultimately proved out was that Powell had become a kind of fall guy, that he had been set up.
sentences.zh: 最终的结果证明，鲍威尔成了一种替罪羊，他被做局了。

sentences.en: He'd been set up perhaps not intentionally by the Bush administration, but ultimately that's what it turned out to be,
sentences.zh: 他被做局了，也许布什政府并非有意为之，但结果最终就是这样，

sentences.en: that he was there presenting intelligence, virtually all of which turned out to be completely false.
sentences.zh: 他当时在作情报报告，而几乎所有这些情报事后证明全都是完全虚假的。

sentences.en: He had, in essence, sold the American public and the international community on a phony pretext for war, with tragic consequences.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，他向美国公众和国际社会兜售了一个虚假的战争借口，造成了悲剧性的后果。

sentences.en: And as he finally comes to understand this, and I know you've talked to him about this, what is his reaction?
sentences.zh: 当他最终明白这一点时，我知道你和他谈过此事，他的反应是什么？

sentences.en: His reaction was horror, anger, and then bitterness.
sentences.zh: 他的反应是震惊、愤怒，然后是痛苦。

sentences.en: And it's worth mentioning also that by the end of 2004,
sentences.zh: 还值得一提的是，到2004年底，

sentences.en: Bush decided he no longer needed Powell's services and replaced him with Condoleezza Rice.
sentences.zh: 布什决定不再需要鲍威尔的服务，由康多莉扎·赖斯取而代之。

sentences.en: In the months and years that followed his departure from the Bush administration...
sentences.zh: 在他离开布什政府后的几个月和几年里……

sentences.en: Writing in his new memoir about your February 5th, 2003 speech to the UN, which has now become historic...
sentences.zh: 他在新回忆录中谈到了你2003年2月5日在联合国的那次演讲，该演讲现已载入史册……

sentences.en: He does a number of interviews...
sentences.zh: 他接受了多次采访……

sentences.en: Are you ticked?
sentences.zh: 你感到恼火吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: ...in which he himself is penitent.
sentences.zh: ……他在采访中表现得很懊悔。

sentences.en: But you held public opinion.
sentences.zh: 但你掌控了公众舆论。

sentences.en: I swayed public opinion.
sentences.zh: 我左右了公众舆论。

sentences.en: There's no question about it.
sentences.zh: 这是毫无疑问的。

sentences.en: ...takes his own lumps, recognizes his own responsibility for this.
sentences.zh: ……他自己承担了责任，意识到了自己对此负有的责任。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: You changed the bulk.
sentences.zh: 你改变了大局。

sentences.en: I changed, I changed, I turned the dial.
sentences.zh: 我改变了，我改变了，我扭转了局面。

sentences.en: There's no question about it.
sentences.zh: 这是毫无疑问的。

sentences.en: As much as it fatigues him to be talking over and over about this singular matter that now appears to be legacy-defining, he does so.
sentences.zh: 尽管一遍又一遍地谈论这个现在看来对其政治遗产具有决定性意义的单一事件让他感到疲惫，但他还是这么做了。

sentences.en: And that's what the president wanted me to do and what I was supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是总统希望我做的，也是我应该做的。

sentences.en: You regret it.
sentences.zh: 你对此感到后悔。

sentences.en: I regret it now because the information was wrong.
sentences.zh: 我现在感到后悔，因为信息是错误的。

sentences.en: Of course I do.
sentences.zh: 我当然后悔。

sentences.en: But I will always be seen as the one who made the case before the international community.
sentences.zh: 但我永远会被视为在国际社会面前陈述这一理由的人。

sentences.en: But there wasn't a word in that...
sentences.zh: 但这里面没有一句话……

sentences.en: Robert, I'm really curious in your conversations with Powell about this war and about his role in selling it,
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，我很想知道你在与鲍威尔关于这场战争以及他在此次兜售中所扮演角色的谈话中，

sentences.en: what kind of responsibility he does or doesn't take for it and for all of its consequences.
sentences.zh: 他为这场战争及其所有后果承担了多少责任，或者根本没有承担责任？

sentences.en: Powell in my conversations with him was pretty defensive on the subject.
sentences.zh: 在我和他的交谈中，鲍威尔对这个话题相当防备。

sentences.en: I mean, the fact that he had been answering so many of these questions over and over again indicated a kind of penitence on his part,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他能够一遍又一遍地回答这么多问题，本身就表明他有一种懊悔，

sentences.en: a recognition that he owed it to history to answer at least semi-serious questions.
sentences.zh: 一种意识到自己至少有责任向历史认真回答半严肃问题的认知。

sentences.en: But that didn't mean that he was going to take responsibility for a war that he believed standing alone among Bush senior officials was inadvisable.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着他要为一场他认为在布什高级官员中独树一帜、不建议发动的战争承担责任。

sentences.en: And he essentially was of the position that, look, I tried to slow it down.
sentences.zh: 他的立场基本上是，听着，我曾试图阻止它发生。

sentences.en: I tried to tell Bush what could go wrong.
sentences.zh: 我曾试图告诉布什可能会出什么问题。

sentences.en: That's basically about as far as Powell would go.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是鲍威尔所能做的极限了。

sentences.en: And I think that he was really of the view that it seemed wrongheaded to suggest that Colin Powell should shoulder so much of the blame for the Iraq debacle
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他的确认为，暗示科林·鲍威尔应该为伊拉克惨败承担那么多责任是极其荒谬的

sentences.en: when he had done more than anybody else in the administration to move it off course.
sentences.zh: 因为他在政府内部比任何人都更能努力将其拉回正轨。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a complicated answer, and it makes me wonder how we should be thinking about his legacy and about this speech all these years later, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个复杂的回答，这让我觉得多年后的今天，我们应该如何看待他的政治遗产和这场演讲，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, in selling a war on false premises, whether he knew they were false or not,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在以虚假借口推销一场战争时，无论他是否知道这些借口是虚假的，

sentences.en: did he ultimately squander this reputation that he had rightfully earned, or was he kind of robbed of it by the people around Bush?
sentences.zh: 他最终是挥霍了他本应得到的声誉，还是被布什身边的人给剥夺了？

sentences.en: Is it the story of this peerless military leader who didn't quite have the courage to stop and stand up to a bad war,
sentences.zh: 这究竟是一个无可匹敌的军事领袖的故事，而他却没有足够的勇气去阻止并挺身对抗一场糟糕的战争，

sentences.en: or is it the story of a man who was a victim of people who were so committed to the war that they were willing to deceive him?
sentences.zh: 还是一个沦为受害者的人的故事，那些人对这场战争如此执着，以至于甘愿欺骗他？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm not going to be the guy who says that this highly decorated military veteran lacked courage.
sentences.zh: 是的，我可不是那种会说这位功勋卓著的退伍军人缺乏勇气的人。

sentences.en: You know, if there's anything I find him particularly guilty of, it's that he was of the same foreign policy establishment
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果说我发现他有什么特别应该受到指责的地方，那就是他属于同一个外交政策建制派

sentences.en: that embraced the same kind of groupthink about Saddam Hussein.
sentences.zh: 他们对萨达姆·侯赛因抱有同一种群体思维。

sentences.en: Powell, in agreeing to give the fateful UN speech, basically was coming in with a view that, yes, Saddam's got weapons.
sentences.zh: 鲍威尔在同意发表那场命运攸关的联合国演讲时，基本上抱有的观点是，是的，萨达姆有武器。

sentences.en: He's got weapons of mass destruction.
sentences.zh: 他拥有大规模杀伤性武器。

sentences.en: And there were plenty of indicators that, at minimum, that baseline judgment needed to be reappraised.
sentences.zh: 有大量的迹象表明，至少那种基准判断需要重新评估。

sentences.en: That Powell didn't do that puts him in the same category, by the way, as then-Senator Hillary Clinton, then-Senator Joe Biden, and an awful lot of other people.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，鲍威尔没有这样做，这使他与当时的参议员希拉里·克林顿、当时的参议员乔·拜登以及其他许多人归为同一类。

sentences.en: His decision not to say to the president, nope, bad idea, I'm resigning.
sentences.zh: 他决定不对总统说，不，这主意太糟了，我要辞职。

sentences.en: I suppose it's fair to make a judgment against Powell for that.
sentences.zh: 我想因此对鲍威尔做出评判是公正的。

sentences.en: But American history is not exactly spangled with instances of generals who stand up to a president in such a manner.
sentences.zh: 但美国历史并不是到处都是将军们以这种方式挺身对抗总统的例子。

sentences.en: And, you know, that presents the complicated, nuanced view of an arguably tragic but heroic figure.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这就展现了一个可以说是悲剧但又是英雄式人物的复杂且充满细微差别的形象。

sentences.en: Why tragic?
sentences.zh: 为什么说是悲剧？

sentences.en: Tragic in the sense that but for his decision to stick with Bush when asked the question, are you with me, and his decision to give the speech that he did.
sentences.zh: 之所以说悲剧，是因为若不是因为当被问到“你跟我在一起吗”时，他决定坚定追随布什，以及他决定发表那场演讲。

sentences.en: But for all of that, Colin Powell would have been viewed as utterly heroic, as someone who was a first in American life in so many ways,
sentences.zh: 如果不是这一切，科林·鲍威尔本会被视为绝对的英雄，一个在许多方面开创美国历史先河的人，

sentences.en: who was so admired as a leader in the State Department, in the military, and who people still speak of, who worked with him in reverential tones.
sentences.zh: 他在国务院和军队中作为领导人备受崇敬，那些曾与他共事过的人至今仍用充满敬意的语气谈论他。

sentences.en: A person who had really lived this seemingly legendary life, but then came Iraq.
sentences.zh: 一个确实经历了这种看似传奇般一生的人，但随后伊拉克战争发生了。

sentences.en: And so he's tragic.
sentences.zh: 所以他是悲剧的。

sentences.en: Robert, I wonder if you could read the first sentence of Colin Powell's obituary
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，我想知道你是否能朗读一下科林·鲍威尔讣告的第一句话

sentences.en: That was published in the Times.
sentences.zh: 那是发表在《时报》上的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The first sentence reads,
sentences.zh: 第一句话是这样的，

sentences.en: This was the obituary he feared.
sentences.zh: 这就是他所恐惧的讣告。

sentences.en: This was the first sentence he did not want.
sentences.zh: 这是他最不希望出现的第一句话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, Powell had, again, tragically, a gift of prophecy here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，同样具有悲剧色彩的是，鲍威尔在这里展现出了一种预言的天赋。

sentences.en: He accurately forecast that this was how he would be remembered.
sentences.zh: 他准确地预测到这就是他会被人们铭记的方式。

sentences.en: Well, Robert, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，罗伯特，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 我们感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: My pleasure, Michael.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸，迈克尔。

sentences.en: On Monday, the family of Colin Powell said he had died from complications of COVID-19, despite being fully vaccinated against the virus.
sentences.zh: 周一，科林·鲍威尔的家人表示，他因新冠肺炎并发症去世，尽管他已经完全接种了该病毒疫苗。

sentences.en: Powell, the family said, was being treated for multiple myeloma, a cancer of the white blood cells that weakens the immune system
sentences.zh: 他的家人说，鲍威尔当时正在接受多发性骨髓瘤的治疗，这是一种削弱免疫系统的白血病

sentences.en: and leaves those with the disease at greater risk of developing severe cases of COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 并使得患有该疾病的人在感染新冠肺炎时面临更高发展为重症的风险。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Monday, former President Donald Trump sued both Congress and the National Archives
sentences.zh: 周一，前总统唐纳德·特朗普对国会和国家档案馆提起诉讼

sentences.en: in an attempt to block them from disclosing White House documents related to the January 6th attack on the U.S.
sentences.zh: 试图阻止他们披露与1月6日美国国会大厦袭击事件相关的白宫文件。

sentences.en: Capitol.
sentences.zh: 国会大厦。

sentences.en: The House committee investigating the attack, which has requested the documents from the National Archives, hopes they will shed light on Trump's role in the assault.
sentences.zh: 正在调查该袭击事件并已向国家档案馆索取这些文件的众议院委员会希望它们能阐明特朗普在这次袭击中的角色。

sentences.en: In the lawsuit, Trump claims that executive privilege protects the documents from congressional review.
sentences.zh: 在这起诉讼中，特朗普声称行政特权保护这些文件免受国会的审查。

sentences.en: And the Times reports that federal regulators are likely to endorse a plan that would allow Americans to receive COVID-19 booster shots that differ from their original vaccines.
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，联邦监管机构很可能会批准一项计划，允许美国人接种与其最初疫苗不同的新冠肺炎加强针。

sentences.en: The ability to mix and match the shots, requested by state health officials, will give doctors and patients greater discretion about which shots to use as boosters.
sentences.zh: 混合接种加强针的能力是应州卫生官员的要求提出的，这将赋予医生和患者更大的自由裁量权，以决定使用哪种加强针。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由卢克·范德普鲁格、斯特拉·谭、悉尼·哈珀和切尔西·丹尼尔制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow and M.J.
sentences.zh: 它由丽莎·周和M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn, engineered by Chris Wood, and contains original music from Marian Lozano and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩编辑，克里斯·伍德担任音频工程，并包含来自玛丽安·洛扎诺和丹·鲍威尔的原创音乐。

sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由旺德利的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯伯格创作。

sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。
